title: Corporate Ethics and Compliance for AI

questions.question: Which feature makes classify_use_case return the prohibited AI Act tier before other sector checks?
options: Social scoring or biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces
A generic internal chatbot with no personal data
A third-party foundation model used for a low-risk drafting task
A public-sector dashboard with an informational recommendation
questions.explanation: The classifier checks is_social_scoring and is_biometric_public_space first. Either flag returns PROHIBITED under the modeled Article 5 rule.

questions.question: What tier does classify_use_case assign to an employment-sector use case without a prohibited feature?
options: MINIMAL
HIGH_RISK
PROHIBITED
The sector is ignored unless the output is a legal decision
questions.explanation: Sector.EMPLOYMENT is in HIGH_RISK_SECTORS. The classifier therefore returns HIGH_RISK even when the use case has no prohibited flag.

questions.question: What does deploys_third_party_foundation_model add to a classification result?
options: It changes every use case to HIGH_RISK
It removes the GDPR triggers because the vendor owns the model
It appends the GPAI provider-obligation note without changing the use case tier
It bypasses the approval gate when the vendor supplies a DPA
questions.explanation: GPAI obligations are attached to the provider axis. classify_use_case appends GPAI_PROVIDER_NOTE to obligations but leaves the Article 6 use-case tier unchanged.

questions.question: A high-risk employment UseCase sends personal data to a third-party model with dpa_signed=False and logging designed. What decision does check_approval_gate return?
options: APPROVED because the classifier already assigned a tier
CONDITIONAL because a missing DPA is only advisory
APPROVED after the model vendor confirms its certification
BLOCKED because the missing DPA is a hard gap for a high-risk use case
questions.explanation: The personal-data API call needs a signed DPA. With a HIGH_RISK result, the not-signed gap is a hard block even if logging is already designed.

questions.question: Which additional GDPR trigger appears when DataType.SPECIAL_CATEGORY is present?
options: An Article 9 basis and a mandatory DPIA are required
No trigger, because special-category data is not personal data
Only a voluntary model-card review is required
The use case is automatically MINIMAL under the AI Act
questions.explanation: classify_use_case adds the special-category trigger requiring an Article 9 exception or consent and states that a DPIA is mandatory.

questions.question: A minimal-risk use case has logging_designed=False and no other gap. What approval decision follows?
options: BLOCKED
CONDITIONAL
APPROVED
PROHIBITED
questions.explanation: For a MINIMAL result, missing logging is recorded as a recommended control gap rather than a high-risk hard block. check_approval_gate therefore returns CONDITIONAL.
